I have been farming this land in Quzhou for 25 years, and I know what the wheat–maize rotation needs on the North China Plain. With 10.1 mu, seven mouths to feed, and some of my family working off-farm, I must save labor where I can and use my well to manage water carefully.

For wheat, I will rotary till the field after the maize harvest in early October and sow an improved variety—something like Jimai 22 or Liangxing that the seed station recommends—at about 15 kg per mu. I will put down basal compound fertilizer before sowing and topdress with urea at green-up in spring. Water is the key to a good wheat crop here, so I will irrigate three times: once before winter to protect the seedlings from the cold, once at jointing when the stems shoot up, and once during grain filling to fill the kernels. Weeds and rust come every year, so I will spray four times—herbicide, fungicide, and insecticide as the crop needs. If the weather is fair, I expect around 500 kg per mu.

For maize, the summer season is short, so timing is everything. Right after I cut the wheat in early June, I will sow hybrid maize—Denghai 605 is what works best around here—using no-tillage to save time and diesel, since my sons are often away working. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing, then irrigate twice: the first when the plants are jointing and the second during grain filling. I will spray four times for weeds and armyworm. With good management, I expect about 550 kg per mu. This is the system that has put food on my table for two decades, and I see no reason to change it.
